title: The atmosphere possibility tables (GEN.478): 16 categories, 104 rows

categories.a: Mantle redox (magma-ocean stage, later upper mantle)
categories.b: Delivered volatile inventory (dry / low / high) and water mass fraction, with snow-line dependence
categories.c: Outgassed atmosphere regime for rocky bodies (L2 under the redox class)
categories.d: Atmospheric retention regime (airless, exosphere, thin, moderate, dense) and primary H/He
categories.e: Sub-Neptune / super-Earth envelope (L1 regime, L2 metallicity)
categories.f: Giant planets: temperature regime, metallicity bins, C/O bins, carbon carrier
categories.g: Brown dwarf spectral-type sequence (BD; free-floating, 13 to 80 MJ)
categories.j: Frost-equilibrium and evolved atmospheres (Titan-, Pluto-, Venus-, Mars-like)
categories.k: Comet and KBO coma volatile classes (ratios to water)
categories.m: Trace and minor gas presence (binary rows: present with probability w, absent with 1-w)
categories.n: Clouds, hazes and dust by temperature window and class
categories.o: Ground radioisotope abundance regimes by host (part 07)

entries.source: Hirschmann 2022 (GCA 328, section 6.3 and Table 1): Fe3+/FeT of the ocean surface 0.034 to 0.103 and the dIW it gives; Deng 2020: the ferric share of the melt against the pressure at the base of the ocean (factor of two from 55 to 25 GPa) and the base pressures; Sossi 2020 0.037 Fe3+/sumFe (READ, COMPUTED); the form, the pressure scaling and the width are DESIGN brackets of docs/design/composition/magma-ocean-redox-model.md
entries.notes: sets the first atmosphere; Fe3+/sumFe 0.037+-0.005; GEN.482 (docs/design/composition/magma-ocean-redox-against-mass.md): the mean is inside the first-hand ranges at the Moon, Mars and Earth, the width and the clamp above 1 Me are not sourced Corrected 2026-10-23 (GEN.479): the gate M >= 0.01 left a body under 0.01 Earth masses with no redox row at all. GEN.1005 (2026-10-30): the mean and width are the model of physics.magma_ocean_redox in place of the line through three Solar System bodies, which are now tests of the model.
entries.limit: the surface redox of the magma ocean from physics.magma_ocean_redox (stand-in rows MR1 to MR7): the base pressure is a power of the mass, held at the 140 GPa where the first-principles calculations end (5.4 Earth masses; no source above), the ferric-share power (0.5 to 1.0) and the offset are read from two papers whose equations were not available when it was built, there is no temperature or composition term, and the graphite-flotation alternative of Gaillard 2022 is not drawn (GEN.482, GEN.1005)

entries.source: the later upper mantle of the rocky bodies measured: dIW +3.5 for the one with plate tectonics (Deng 2020 with its refs 37, 6, 7; Hirschmann 2022 section 4: above IW+3), IW to IW+1 for the primitive mantle of the next lighter one and IW to IW-2 for the lightest (Hirschmann 2022 introduction and section 4; Deng 2020 refs 8 to 10); the increment, its growth with mass and the width 1.0 are DESIGN (READ, COMPUTED; docs/design/composition/magma-ocean-redox-model.md)
entries.notes: far above meteoritic building blocks (part 05 s3.2); GEN.482 (docs/design/composition/magma-ocean-redox-against-mass.md): inside one standard deviation of the three first-hand anchors, no source above 1 Me GEN.1005 (2026-10-30): the mean is the magma-ocean model's surface value plus the increment, in place of the straight line through three Solar System bodies; GEN.482b takes the larger of a2 and a1 in `draw_redox`.
entries.limit: the magma-ocean surface of the body (physics.magma_ocean_redox, at most that of one Earth mass) plus an oxidation increment of 1.2 to 2.4 that grows with the mass: a line between two numbers (stand-in row MR7), not a model of the oxidation (hydrogen loss, lower-mantle disproportionation, recycling); the sources give a gap of 0 to 3 that grows with mass; the later mantle is never below the magma-ocean surface of the same body (GEN.482, GEN.482b, GEN.1005)
